vignette: A 63-year-old man is brought by his daughter because he has become apathetic, sits all day and answers in monosyllables since a stroke two weeks ago. He is fully oriented and has no weakness. MRI shows a small infarct in the head of the caudate nucleus and the anterior limb of the internal capsule.

options.text: Anterior thalamic radiation and prefrontal-striatal loop

explanation: The anterior limb carries the anterior thalamic radiation between the mediodorsal and anterior thalamus and the prefrontal cortex, and the caudate head is the striatal station of the prefrontal loop; their interruption produces abulia without weakness, the frontal picture of a medial lenticulostriate (Heubner) infarct.
